# Resource: widget_gadget

A gadget. `terraform destroy` deletes it.

~> A gadget can move real money. In a live-mode account, creating or changing one fails at plan time.

~> Gadgets cannot be deleted. `terraform destroy`, and a change that would replace the gadget, fail at plan time. To stop managing a gadget, remove it from the state as [Removing from State](#removing-from-state) shows; it stays in the account.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "widget_gadget" "main" {
  name = "Main"
}
```

### With parts

```terraform
resource "widget_gadget" "parts" {
  name = "Parts"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are required:

* `name` - (Required) Name of the gadget.

The following arguments are optional:

* `legacy` - (Optional, Deprecated) An old field. Default: none.
* `note` - (Optional) A note. Changing it replaces the resource. Default (Stripe): `draft`. Removing it from the configuration leaves the current value.
* `parts` - (Optional) The parts of the gadget. See [`parts`](#parts) below.
* `password` - (Optional, Write-Only) A password the provider never stores.
* `reference` - (Optional) A reference only an update sets. Default: not sent.
* `tier` - (Optional) The pricing tier. Default (Stripe): the account's default tier (`basic` on a US account).
* `token` - (Optional, Sensitive) A token that stays in state.

<a id="parts"></a>
### `parts`

The `parts` attribute is a list. Each element supports:

* `label` - (Required) Label of the part.
* `options` - (Optional) Options of the part. See [`parts.options`](#parts.options) below.
* `serial` - (Read-Only) Serial number, set by the API.

<a id="parts.options"></a>
### `parts.options`

The `parts.options` attribute is a map. Each value supports:

* `finish` - (Optional) Finish of the option. See [`parts.options.finish`](#parts.options.finish) below.
* `size` - (Required) Size of the option.

<a id="parts.options.finish"></a>
### `parts.options.finish`

The `parts.options.finish` attribute supports:

* `colour` - (Optional) Colour of the finish. Default: none.

## Attribute Reference

This resource exports the following attributes in addition to the arguments above:

* `id` - Unique identifier for the object.
* `history` - What happened to the gadget. See [`history`](#history) below.
* `last_part` - The part attached last. See [`last_part`](#last_part) below.
* `status` - The status of the gadget.

<a id="history"></a>
### `history`

The `history` attribute is a set. Each element supports:

* `at` - When it happened.
* `secret` - (Sensitive) A secret detail.

<a id="last_part"></a>
### `last_part`

The `last_part` attribute holds a widget gadget part, with the attributes of the [`widget_gadget_part`](../data-sources/widget_gadget_part) data source and `object`, the name of its type.

## Timeouts

[Configuration options](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/syntax#operation-timeouts) are set with the `timeouts` attribute, for example `timeouts = { create = "5m" }`:

* `create` - (Default `20m`)
* `delete` - (Default `20m`)
* `update` - (Default `20m`)

## Removing from State

To stop managing a widget gadget whose destroy is refused, remove it from the state without destroying it. In Terraform 1.7 and later, and OpenTofu 1.10 and later, replace the `resource` block with a [`removed` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/removed) and apply:

```terraform
removed {
  from = widget_gadget.main

  lifecycle {
    destroy = false
  }
}
```

Using `terraform state rm`:

```console
% terraform state rm widget_gadget.main
```

The widget gadget stays in the Stripe account. Replacing one with `terraform apply -replace` or `terraform taint` fails in the same way, at apply.

## Import

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, and in OpenTofu, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import a widget gadget using its ID. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = widget_gadget.main
  id = "gad_123"
}
```

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, and in OpenTofu v1.12.0 and later, the `import` block can use the `identity` attribute instead. For example:

```terraform
import {
  to = widget_gadget.main
  identity = {
    id = "gad_123"
  }
}
```

### Identity Schema

#### Required

* `id` (String) The Stripe ID of the widget gadget.

Using `terraform import`, import a widget gadget using its ID. For example:

```console
% terraform import widget_gadget.main gad_123
```

~> An imported gadget has no `token`.
